subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw design a gateway-side credential-forwarding flow for this command?
rationale: Both choices change where sensitive provider OAuth material may be acquired and stored, and automation should not choose that credential boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with a gateway-host instruction and preserve loopback or SSH-tunnel setups through shared loopback semantics.

options.title: Design credential forwarding
options.body: Add an authenticated gateway-side flow that moves provider auth material into the gateway store without consuming tokens into the node-local store first.

options.title: Warn but allow
options.body: Keep the permissive local write path but tell node-host users it will not update the gateway, accepting the current wrong-host credential risk for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with a gateway-host instruction and preserve loopback or SSH-tunnel setups through shared loopback semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This person already authored and verified the maintainer repair direction for the exact remote-node auth guard.
